title: Initial evaluation, low back, night-shift nurse

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Lena, welcome. Tell me what's going on with your low back.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I work nights as a nurse. For about four months it's been sore low in the back, around 4 to 5 out of 10.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Lifting patients is the worst part. Sitting in the car after a shift is bad too.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any pain that goes into the buttock or down the leg?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Sometimes the buttock, but never past the knee.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any numbness, bowel or bladder changes, or fever?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: I'll do the hip and back strength test at the next visit, since we ran out of time today.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Badly. I get about five hours in the day, and back pain wakes me up.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Assessment: the back pain is worse with lifting and sitting, and it's affecting your sleep. Plan: start a hinge pattern drill and a sitting-break routine.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: I'll see you again in one week, and I'll check the strength then.

expectedFacts.statement: Low back sore for about four months, 4 to 5 out of 10
Lifting patients is the worst part
Sleeps about five hours a day
Back pain wakes the patient up
Pain worse with lifting and sitting, affecting sleep
Hinge pattern drill and sitting-break routine
